title: Merchant Banking stays at arm’s length from Core/Retail
summary: Merchant Banking owns derivative contracts, valuation, exposure, margin, collateral requirements, default, close-out and contractual settlement obligations. It does not own Core asset existence, ownership, legal control or Retail/Core Ledger posting.
invariants: Merchant Banking is a separate regulatory/authority perimeter, not a module inside Core Banking.
Core-held assets contribute zero Merchant collateral value until explicit enforceable Core control evidence exists.
Merchant may create a contractual settlement obligation; that is not a Retail Ledger movement.
A Merchant position projection may be displayed by a channel but does not become Retail available balance.
A common beneficial owner or Retail linkage does not collapse legal entities or relationships.

provenance.claim: Merchant Banking is arm-length from Core and has no Retail/Core Ledger posting API.
Merchant close-out obligation is not a Retail Ledger movement and position projection does not imply Retail available balance.
